note: A laptop size of issue #114: it trains on one RTX 5080 Laptop GPU in about 15 minutes and shows whether the code works. 1.9M parameters without the vocabulary's two tables, 10.3M with them (width 64, 11 layers: two window layers on each side of an exact layer, then one exact layer and five sparse layers), the balanced dataset's 65,536-token vocabulary and 32K-token windows. It reads the first 81,920,000 tokens of a corpus of 1,179,648,000, the size patient-tortoise reads, so one corpus serves the three laptop sizes: 500 updates of 5 windows, a warm-up of 20. The time assumes 100,000 tokens/s (estimated from the 45,550 tokens/s measured for 21 layers of width 128, not measured); `wpt train --stop-after-minutes` measures it. Its shape, learning rate and batch follow eldest-titmouse's laws at this width, but its tokens are set by the time, far below what the laws ask. Its 11 layers are outside the series: a setting found on it is checked again at 21 layers before it is kept. Untested in a full run.
